results.content:
The problem

Every ecommerce team runs the same loop: brief a creative, wait a week, launch the ad, watch it flop. Rework the hook, relaunch, burn more budget. By the time something finally sticks, the trend has moved on.

What kept bugging me is that the winning ad usually already exists. It’s running in your market right now, and a competitor is paying to prove it works. That’s a research problem, not a creativity problem, but everyone keeps solving it with more creativity.

⚡ What we built

Wisry is an autonomous execution layer for paid ads. You give it your store, and its AI agents run what we call a Campaign Run:

- Competitor Intel: reverse-engineers the ads already winning in your market

- Research-based angles: hooks and messages, each with the evidence behind it [...] Ruta Jaskunaite

@sansa\_grey Fair concern, and honestly the reason we built it the way we did.

Wisry doesn't copy the visuals. It reads the structure of the ad that's working: the hook, the pacing, where the proof lands, how it closes. Then it rebuilds that around your product, your footage or avatar, your palette, your script. Two brands cloning the same source ad end up with two different ads that share a skeleton.

The other thing is the research citation. You see which ads it drew from, so if everyone in your niche is running the same format, you can pick a different source, or have it fan out hook variants instead. [...] Amy Bradley

Does the system adjust the creative when the original winning ad targets a very different customer segment?

Ruta Jaskunaite

@amybradley Good question. Yes, partly by design and partly by you.

Wisry starts from your store, not the source ad. It reads your products and who you sell to first, and that brand profile is what the script, the avatar and the visuals get built against. So what carries over from the source ad is the structure (hook, pacing, proof, close), not the audience or the message.

# Why Ad Cloning Beats Creating Ads From Scratch

Creating ads from scratch means starting with a guess. Ad cloning starts from angles already winning in your market and turns them into branded creative you can launch and measure. This is why it works.

14 Aug 2026
|
7 min read

A marketer comparing an original competitor ad and a freshly redesigned branded version pinned side by side on an office mood board

In this article

Share

Most ecommerce brands build ad creative the same way: open a blank document, brainstorm hooks, brief a designer, run it, and hope. Every decision in that process is a guess. [...] Template generation fills your product details into a pre-built layout based on generic best practices. The premise is unvalidated. Ad cloning starts from a specific structure proven in your market by a competitor’s spend. The starting point is fundamentally different, and so is the quality of the first draft.

Written by: The Wisry Team

## Turn the next idea into an ad

Research the market, shape the creative and move into production in one focused workflow.

## Also recommended

A modern server room with blue-lit racks and an engineer reviewing system data on a tablet

### Inside the Wisry Agent Runtime: One Engine Behind Every Agent [...] ## How Wisry runs this loop

Wisry’s Competitor Intel runs a research agent across the Meta and TikTok ad libraries, reads the ads it finds for structural arguments (hook type, awareness stage, objection, proof, offer), groups the recurring patterns, and returns six campaign angles for your brand. Each angle traces back to the competitor ad it was built from.

From those angles, Wisry generates static and video ads in your brand, pushes them into Meta and Google campaigns, and runs the optimisation loop, monitoring toward ROAS and flagging what to scale or retire. The manual steps between research and launched ad are gone.

The claim check runs at the brief stage: competitor assertions get flagged before they become your copy, so what ships is grounded in your own product facts.
